Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
25 pages, 15 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models run the same block of layers several times for every token. They use the same number of loops to read the prompt (prefill) and to write each new token (decode). But when a model writes a chain of thought, almost all of the time goes into decoding. On Ouro-2.6B at batch 1, prefill takes only 0.4-2.6% of the time. So at small batch sizes, extra prefill loops cost little time. We untie the two loop counts. We read the prompt with more loops and decode with fewer. The original model cannot use a prompt read with more loops, so we distill a small adapter (2.4% of the parameters). For a fixed prefill depth, LoRA on the decoder is enough. LoopBridge adds small key and value maps, so that one adapter serves every trained pair of loop counts and still retrieves facts from 16K-token prompts. On Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, four prefill loops lift the average over 11 benchmarks from 44.2 to 58.6 with the fixed-depth adapter (58.2 with LoopBridge). Both scores are well above the original model distilled to one loop on the same data (49.5). On four chain-of-thought tasks, our models take 14-21% more time per request than the original model with one loop and are 17-19 points more accurate. Two to five prefill loops give most of the gain. The gain holds on Ouro-1.4B, on the Thinking models and on looped decision models. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/untying-prefill-decode
